items.stem: In a mathematics test, Amina scores 34 out of 40.

parts.t: Write Amina’s mark as a percentage.

Bilal scores 65% in the same test.
Work out Bilal’s mark.

sols: write the score as a fraction of the total, then multiply by 100

items.stem:
A jacket has a normal price of $80.
In a sale, the price of the jacket is reduced by 15%.

parts.t: Work out the sale price of the jacket.

sols: Alternative: the sale price is 100 − 15 = 85% of $80, so 0.85 × 80 = $68

items.stem:
Rashid buys a car for $12 500.
Three years later he sells the car for $9750.
sols: the percentage change is always compared with the original amount

items.stem:
The price of a mobile phone is increased by 20%.
The new price is $432.

parts.t: Calculate the price of the phone before the increase.

sols: After a 20% increase the new price is 120% of the original price.
120% of the original price = 432, so 1.2 × original = 432
the multiplier for a 20% increase is 1.2
divide by the multiplier — do not take 20% off $432
ms:
M1 for 432 associated with 120% oe
M1 for 432 ÷ 1.2 oe
A1
cao; 345.6 scores 0

items.stem:
There are 960 students in a school.
55% of these students are boys.

parts.t: Work out the number of girls in the school.

25% of the girls play hockey.
Work out the number of girls who play hockey.

sols: the two percentages must add up to 100%
25% is the same as one quarter

items.stem: Nadia invests $2400 in an account paying 3.5% per year compound interest.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of her investment at the end of 4 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Work out the total interest she earns in these 4 years.

sols: The multiplier for one year is 1 + <sup>3.5</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> = 1.035.
each year the money is 103.5% of the amount at the start of that year
ms:
M1 for 1.035 seen as a multiplier
M1 for 2400 × 1.0354 oe
A1
accept 2754.055… ; 2754 alone scores M2A0

items.stem:
In a sale, the price of a laptop is reduced by 12%.
The sale price of the laptop is $528.

parts.t: Calculate the price of the laptop before the sale.

After the sale, the shop increases the sale price of $528 by 12%.
Work out this new price.

sols: A 12% reduction leaves 100 − 12 = 88% of the original price.
0.88 is the multiplier for a 12% decrease
increasing by 12% does not undo a 12% decrease, because the 12% is now taken of a smaller amount
ms:
M1 for 528 associated with 88% oe
M1 for 528 ÷ 0.88 oe
A1
cao; 591.36 scores 0

items.stem:
A van is bought for $24 000.
Its value depreciates by 18% of its value at the start of each year.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of the van at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the overall percentage decrease in the value of the van over these 3 years.

sols: Each year the van keeps 100 − 18 = 82% of its value, so the multiplier is 0.82.
exact value $13 232.83 to the nearest cent
Overall multiplier = 0.82<sup>3</sup> = 0.551368, so the value left is 55.1368% of the original.
not 3 × 18 = 54%, because each 18% is of a smaller amount
ms:
M1 for 0.82 seen as a multiplier
M1 for 24000 × 0.823 oe
A1
accept 13232.8… or 13232.83

items.stem:
A shopkeeper buys 120 shirts at $14 each.
She sells 90 of the shirts at a profit of 45% each.
She sells the remaining shirts at cost price.

parts.t: Work out the selling price of one of the 90 shirts.
Calculate the total amount of money she receives for all 120 shirts.
Calculate her percentage profit on the 120 shirts.

sols: a 45% profit means the multiplier is 1.45
compare the profit with the total cost price

items.stem:
Mrs Osei buys a house for $180 000.
In the first year the value of the house increases by 6%.
In the second year the value increases by a further 4%.

parts.t: Calculate the value of the house at the end of the second year.
Calculate the overall percentage increase in the value of the house over the two years.

During the third year the value falls, so that at the end of the third year the house is worth $180 000 again.
Calculate the percentage decrease in the third year.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: not 6 + 4 = 10%, because the 4% is taken of the larger amount
the decrease is compared with the value at the start of the third year
